summary: NemesisGaming: regenerate retry loop caused runaway token billing and session duplication during prod spike
description: Issue summary: During a high-traffic window on 2026-03-05, Nemesis Gaming observed explosive token usage and duplicated completions for a subset of streaming chat requests. Impact: Customer-facing gaming features saw inflated billing (estimated 12x baseline token consumption for affected sessions) and duplicate responses leading to a partial rollback of game chat features by the customer. Environment: Production (us-west-2), Nemesis Gaming enterprise account using dedicated capacity with model redwood/gpt-16k-1.2B-quant. Initial alert: Automated billing delta monitor alerted at 2026-03-05T03:22Z. Customers contacted Support at 03:30Z. Summary of customer impact: users experienced repeated regenerated completions and short-lived session loops; Nemesis temporarily disabled inference calls in-game to stop costs.

steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use the Redwood Node SDK v2.4.1 with streaming enabled and regenerate-on-silence enabled
2) Initiate a chat session with short turn timeouts (client-side 800ms) and high request fanout (10 concurrent sessions per user),
3) Trigger a control-plane config flip that temporarily sets streaming reconnect backoff to 'immediate' (this was performed during a canary rollout),
4) Observe client reconnects issuing new completion calls while prior requests still in flight — server treats them as independent requests and charges tokens for each completion.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: client SDK resend bug creating duplicate independent requests when reconnect backoff is misconfigured
Hypothesis B: control-plane partially propagated new backoff policy to a subset of api-gateway nodes leading to inconsistent behavior across nodes

Finding: Traffic capture and node-level config snapshots show that ~30% of gateway nodes received the new backoff policy early, causing immediate reconnects from clients that hit those nodes; SDK v2.4.1 doesn't deduplicate in-flight regenerate calls
Metric evidence: spike in reconnects per session correlated with increase in duplicate request_ids and roughly 11x token billing for affected sessions
Reproducibility: reproduced in staging by flipping backoff policy during a steady fanout and using SDK v2.4.1 — produced duplicate completions and increased token counts
resolution_summary: Mitigations applied: 1) Immediate: enforced per-account temporary rate cap for Nemesis and rolled back the canary backoff change at 03:50Z. 2) Short-term: published SDK guidance to disable aggressive regenerate-on-silence for v2.4.1 and provided a hotfix to the client SDK dedup logic. 3) Fix: control-plane config propagation bug patched (PR merged) and canary rollout process updated to validate node-level config parity prior to backoff policy changes. Billing remediation: issued a credit covering the incremental token delta for the incident window and provided granular token usage export to the customer. Incident declared resolved after monitoring showed normalized token rates for 72 hours.
postincident_actions: Action 1: Add control-plane parity check to rollout pipeline (owner: infra-ops). Due: 2026-03-20
Action 2: Add server-side idempotency key handling for regenerate calls to prevent double-billing for concurrent reconnects (owner: serving-runtime). Due: 2026-04-02
Action 3: Release SDK v2.4.2 hotfix with dedup logic and clear changelog; coordinate with SDK maintainers and customer engineering. Due: 2026-03-10 (completed)
Action 4: Create automated customer-facing billing transparency export for enterprise accounts to detect anomalous token ramps (owner: billing). Due: 2026-03-31
Action 5: Update runbooks for Support to immediately apply per-account emergency caps and sunny-day rollback steps (owner: Support). Due: 2026-03-15
